text: From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-3/RLN-4 checks): the same model, prompt and per-request seeds on a different GPU moves a 500-problem score by about 3 points, so compare cells only with paired intervals and never read a difference of a few points between hardware as an effect. Base Olmo-3-1025-7B, plain prompt, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, vLLM 0.32.0, seeds 1,000,000 + index: n13 on L40S vs RLN-3 base-01 on RTX PRO 6000: 176 of 500 texts identical, scores equal on 436 of 500 (43 of the first 50); grader v1 286 vs 302 (+3.2 points), v3 305 vs 319. Cued base, problems 0-49, H100 vs RTX PRO 6000: scores equal on 42 of 50, 8 texts identical, 35 vs 37 right, 11 vs 9 cap hits. RL, problems 0-49, H200 vs L40S: scores equal on 48 of 50. Iterate-hack's Day-1 check (H100 vs L40S, T1 cell) fits this: 43 vs 40 right, 7 of 50 identical. vLLM is also not batch-invariant, so running a cell alone vs in a large batch changes texts too. The frozen pass thresholds (>= 45 of 50 same GPU, >= 38 other GPU, stop < 30; empty answers give 13 of 50) came from these numbers. Status: closed, measured. Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/SPEC4.md sections 0 and 6, rln4/modal_k-01/readout.json (check), rln4/modal_t2-01/check_rl.json, SPEC3.md section 10 (G-CHECK 60.4 v1).

From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 grader v3 limits): two known ways grader v3 errs, and the format split behind most v1 misses. (1) A mid-line 'Answer:' marker also matches when the model invents and answers a new problem after its real answer; that is the only right-to-wrong flip of 114 over 9 cells (plain base T 1.0, problem 146: v1 right, v3 takes 'Answer: $60$' of an invented COFFEE problem). (2) A tail of three or more letters glued to a number is cut even when it is a product of variables ('2xyz' becomes '2'). v3 checks: 500/500 golds equal themselves, 3 equal after a derangement, planted pairs 24/24 and 16/16, 22 audited rows. Why v1 failed: the base ends with an 'Answer:' line in 39-46 % of answers and RL boxes (n13: 'Answer:' line share base 0.44, RL 0.00); v1/v2 found no answer in 166 of 500 plain-base T 1.0 answers and 127 of 500 plain-base T 0.6 answers. This format difference is also what drives the RLN-5 log-prob gap at the answer start (result-fdc8da). The v1 -> v3 flip counts are already on the board (knowledge-781efc). Status: closed, one reader; no second model has read the v3 rescoring (open). Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/rln4/grader_v3/readout.json (flip_review), rln4_grader_v3_test.py, SPEC4.md 'Grader v3'.

From interp_research next (01_JLENS.md, 22_JLENS_MECHANISM_LITERATURE.md): J-lens follow-ups that add to result-da11d0. interp_research read 2607.15495 in full (all appendices); the follow-ups carry the readers' own tags, given here; [full] for 22_ means methods and results read, with 11 deciding quotes rechecked.
Steering with lens vectors is weak on open models:
- Nanda, Qwen 3.6 27B, 25 prompts (LessWrong + commentary PDF, [full]): verbal-report swaps 'weak but positive'; poetry and arithmetic swaps 'failed to replicate'; multi-hop answer swaps 'strictly dominate' intermediate swaps.
- Zeisler, Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma 3 27B-it (LessWrong, [partial]): intermediate swaps flip top-1 on 6.3-11.1 % (2/32, 4/44, 2/28, 3/27).
- Tang, 8 open models (LessWrong, [full]): the answer-plane part of a swap gives 26 % of its flips, the orthogonal part 12 %; in 65 % neither part alone flips.
- Mazaheri 2608.15022 ([full] in 22_, [abstract] in 01_): three components move the lens readout to within 12 % of each other but differ 7.4x in effect on the answer. Readout is not effect.
- Merlo, Head-JLens, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ([full]): swap at 64 heads 57/140 vs 0/140 random heads; site chosen knowing the answer.
- First-order prediction underestimates steering: Young (LessWrong, [full]) 23-47 % of the actual effect at strength 1; LRE 2308.09124 ([partial]) 2.5x-4.3x.
- The paper's only dose point: target top-1 76/192 at alpha 1, 101/192 at alpha 2 (Sec 3.4). Its steering vector = unit lens row x layer mean residual norm x strength.
Base vs RL and errors:
- Luthra (LessWrong, [partial]): on a reward-hacking Qwen3-8B organism, J-lens readouts were similar across checkpoints despite different behaviour. A prior for a small diff in work-50d329.
- Lens signals that predict errors, abstracts only: 2610.22636 (minimum J-lens steering that changes the output is smaller for wrong answers); 2610.28187 (J-lens features predict test failures, ROC-AUC +0.14). Relevant to idea-f3b647.
- The one patch that raised accuracy: Shi 2611.01519 (second reader, not rechecked): patching the model's own bridge-entity representation at early-middle layers lifts two-hop accuracy 0.03-0.06 -> 0.20-0.26 in three 7-8B models.
Prediction to register for a lens diff of RL - base (03_IDEAS.md N24, draft): the change loads on end-of-answer tokens, and clamping those coordinates removes most of the gain; refuted if it loads on numbers and operations. Floors to use (01_JLENS.md): matched-norm random direction, J under a fixed random rotation, irrelevant same-category swap.

From interp_research next (01_JLENS.md, 22_JLENS_MECHANISM_LITERATURE.md, 04_RECENT.md): J-lens assets for Olmo 3, and a correction to knowledge-0220f1. Status: model cards and READMEs read; no lens below was loaded or tested by interp_research.
- Lenses for the RL models may already exist: HF mhough/olmo3-jacobian-lenses (created 2026-07-22, updated 2026-10-22) lists lenses for Olmo-3-1025-7B base, Instruct SFT/DPO/final, Think SFT/DPO/final and 'four RL-Zero models', layers 0, 3, ..., 30 (04_RECENT.md, card only). knowledge-0220f1 says none exists for the RL model. Check whether its RL-Zero-Math lens is the 3.0 or the 3.1 model before use. The same repo reports refit cosines of 0.884 at layer 0 rising to 1.000 at layer 30 (22_, quote checked): the ceiling for comparing two lenses.
- The neuronpedia Olmo-3-1025-7B lens targets the FINAL block (its config.yaml sets no target layer; library default n_layers - 1), not the penultimate block. File 1,040,198,095 bytes, fp16, 31 source layers of 4096 x 4096. Brauer (LessWrong, DeepSeek-V3, [partial]): a final-block target inherits one direction amplified ~12x by the last block (43 % of J's squared norm at layer 0); about half of mid-depth readouts turn mostly Chinese; a penultimate target cuts this ~20x; 80 % of 78 released lenses target the final block. Fit a penultimate-target lens beside it.
- jeeva2812/olmo3-jlens-checkpoints (HF, [partial]): Olmo 3 7B lenses at stage-1 steps 0 to 1,413,814 and stage 2, layer 20. One massive-activation direction carried 53-99.8 % of variance and caused a retracted claim: project out the top 1-3 massive dimensions before reading a base-vs-RL difference.
- Tokenizer (checked by interp_research on allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B tokenizer.json, 2026-11-04): every string '0'-'999' is one token, no 4-digit string is, and a leading space is a separate token. So every intermediate below 1000 has its own lens vector (Qwen splits digits; J++ could not test arithmetic there).
- Rohweder 2610.27241, entity lens on Olmo-3-7B, layer 17 ([full] in 22_, quote checked): 'The anchor captures the relation. A foreign subject term leaves the answer largely intact'; relation-agnostic score vs LRE faithfulness rho 0.7355 over 28 relations ([abstract]).
- Cost: fitting one lens for a 7B model at 25 prompts x 128 tokens is about 3e17 FLOP, 0.5-1 GPU-h on one L40S (estimate, not measured). github.com/anthropics/jacobian-lens has fitting and readout only; swap, ablation and gradient pursuit must be written.
- Others: senku21x/olmo3-32b-jacobian-lens-checkpoints (32B think-sft, think-dpo, think); danorel/Olmo-3-7B-Instruct-jpp-lens (J++).

From interp_research next (04_RECENT.md, 04_LITERATURE.md, 04_PRACTICAL.md, 04_WDD.md): literature on what RL and fine-tuning change in the weights, not yet in team memory. None was read line by line: [full] in 04_RECENT means methods and results read from HTML/PDF and the rest searched; TEXT in 04_LITERATURE means only the passage for the claim was read.
- 2610.37719 Shiromani, 'What a Weight Update Buys' ([full]): leverage = Fisher quadratic form of an update / that of random directions of the same size, on Olmo-3-7B checkpoints incl. five RL-Zero runs. Pretraining windows 0.78-0.95, SFT 5.4-5.7, RL-Zero and RLVR 388-1,508, DPO 3,304-6,165. Whole model only. For work-d36669: a random difference of matched norm should have hundreds of times less effect; report its Fisher leverage beside its score.
- 2609.15064 Du et al., fixed-SAE track ([full]): one SAE over base + 13 GRPO checkpoints, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, layer 27. Drift small and late-layer; steering the changed features into the base recovers about 80 % of the RL gain.
- 2610.22937 Gupta et al. ([full]): swapping the attention patterns of six middle layers between the RL and DPO checkpoints of OLMo-2-7B and Tulu-3-8B moves a suggested-answer cue effect 'most of the way' to the other checkpoint's level.
- 2604.13694 Weight Patching (TEXT): instruct -> base patching on Llama 3.2 3B, 3.1 8B, 2 13B; 'down-only localization is markedly weaker; restoration is strongest when gate and up are combined'; top 5 % of heads and neurons recover 'a substantial portion' of instruction following (figures only).
- 2509.04259 RL's Razor (TEXT): 'the same training with float32 resulted in models with identical performance but without any sparsity in their weight updates' (second source for the bf16 point); forward KL predicts forgetting (R^2 0.96 MNIST, 0.71 Qwen2.5-3B) better than weight-change size (0.34-0.58, MNIST).
- 2607.20952 chess RL, LoRA Qwen3-14B (TEXT): 86.2 % of RL weight-change energy in MLP projections, 56.5 % in gate_proj, 13.8 % in attention.
- 2302.06600 Panigrahi (TEXT; RoBERTa-base, GPT-2 small): ~0.01 % of parameters grafted by a learned mask carry > 95 % of fine-tuning performance, but ranking by movement |theta_ft - theta_pre| does worse than a learned mask, and AdamW fine-tuning 'does not contain sparse grafted models with good performance' without an l1 penalty. Consistent with N13 (knowledge-8229be).
- Abstracts only: 2610.22438 (counted rank of 13 released updates up to 8B only a little below a random matrix of the same shape); 2609.22146 GRRR (removing the change of singular values keeps most math gains); 2609.36262 (fixed sparse masks from the initial diagonal Fisher keep a large share of the RL gain); 2606.26474 (one crosscoder feature for RL tool use, Qwen2.5-3B, transfer to base +6.8 +- 5.0 pp); 2609.00925 (adding the starting model's grounding direction recovers 35 % of the DPO gain); 2611.02574 (OLMo-2-1B, 13 RLVR checkpoints: pass@1 58.0 -> 61.3 %, coverage at 256 samples 94.5 -> 96.9 %).
- Caution from 04_WDD (one-author GitHub program, Pythia-410m, step 16000 parts into step 8000): every transplant closure was negative (whole neuron -0.020, 512 neurons with direction -0.066, readout -0.873): mixing parts of two checkpoints moved the model away from the donor. Measure transplants in both directions.
- Citation check (04_LITERATURE.md): RelP is 2508.21258 (Rezaei Jafari et al.); 2601.22594 is Arora et al., 'Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis'; knowledge-9d0f85 attaches RelP to 2601.22594.

Weight-space programming edit (interp_research studies/instruments, exploratory, gate cancelled): the released Qwen3.5-0.8B loop edit is the released change's top singular vector u per block, rebuilt as W <- W - 6 u(u^T W) on 64 down_proj columns (relative Frobenius error 0.0012). Reduction of the repetition share R = 0.317 for the edit vs 0.080-0.093 for random columns (300 MATH-500 answers per arm, cap 8,192); accuracy rises with any edit that shortens answers (cap-censored, base 0.047). results/RESULTS.md items 22-27.

cleanneurons Part I (what the neurons do), Olmo 3 base. (1) Of the 100 MLP neurons whose copy from RL moves the base most (Part T2), 44 are on almost everywhere (|a| beyond the layer p97 at > 50 % of 131,397 positions) vs 1 of 100 layer-matched random neurons; median mean |a| 0.213 vs 0.020; their gate/up/down weights have cosine 1.0000 with RL's. Reading: RL's effect rides on always-on neurons, where a tiny weight change adds nearly the same vector everywhere; a constant-push arm is being tested. (2) Blind description test (Goodfire-style detection): a reader writes one sentence per neuron from 10 top contexts; a second reader, with the sentence only, picks the 10 firing snippets out of 20 (10 held-out top contexts + 10 random positions of the same answers). Accuracy: 90.7 % [86.0, 94.7] for 30 of the best neurons, 71.3 % [60.0, 81.3] for 15 random neurons, chance 50 %. So single neurons of this 7B model are describable at their peaks. Limits: peaks only; writer and tester are the same LLM. Jobs sameraslan-1114-154532-cdc8 (H100, 48 s). Literature from interp_research, 30 papers read in full, 147 findings in past.dev (recall.py). What bears on the direction: (1) RL gain is sparse in tokens and re-weights base behavior: swapping the RL token at 4-8% of positions lifts base AIME24 to RL level, RL token is in base top-3 >80% (2603.22446); RL keeps the base's forking positions, 86.7% overlap (2506.01939); base Olmo-3-7B already writes 'wait' ~5/1k, RL-Zero-Math 76.5/1k at T 0.6 with 29.1% length-limit hits vs 17.8% base (2610.30882); URIAL: 92% of chat tokens in base top-3, shift at the start (2312.01552). Spurious rewards help only where the behavior exists; OLMo2 flat (2506.10947). (2) Weight difference: rank-1 of the RL update, rescaled, keeps ~100% of MATH-500 gain, lambda peak ~0.7 (2510.00553); update x0.75 +3.4 GSM8K, matched-norm random update 59.5->5% (2610.22438); Olmo-3 RL-Zero leverage 708x random, carried by signs; x1.5 breaks stopping (stop rate to 0.005-0.18) (2610.37719); top 0.1% Fisher mask gives 85% of RL gain vs random 23.9 (2609.36262); RL update is rotation not rescaling, incl. OLMo-3 Think-RL (2609.22146); DARE needs deltas <=~0.002, fails >0.01 (2311.03099); Bolmo moves an Olmo-3 RL-Zero IF delta to a byte model, IFEval 31.1->67.4 (2512.15586); 13 params give 74.6 vs 78.2 full on MATH-500 (2602.04118). Fine-tune sparsity is bf16 rounding, gone in fp32 (2509.04259). (3) Loops: loop onset = entropy drops to ~0 after a Wait/But burst, probe flags 64-76% ~1,500 tokens early (2601.05693); Olmo-3-7B-Think cap hits only 62% loops (2611.06095); loop-neuron edits beat random in 4/8 cells and can turn loops into endless reasoning (2606.13705); repetition-neuron ablation fixes ~30% (2410.13497). (4) Decode-time/steering: SEAL keyword-labeled vector, R1-Distill-7B MATH-500 85.8->89.4 with -21% tokens (2504.07986); proxy-tuning on first tokens only fails (base falls back to repetition) (2401.08565); forced Wait barely moves MATH500 (2501.19393); SAE steering recovers format, not reasoning (2609.15064). Plus 25 board items of interp_research's own results (knowledge-9c5052...). work-02efb7

cleanneurons Part T3 (is the RL change a constant push?), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math, held-out 2,672 decisive positions after the cue (T1 text / T2 text): adding ONE constant vector per layer to the base (mean of RL-layer minus base-layer output, 32 vectors, no weight change) closes 23.4 / 31.2 % of KL(RL||base); a random vector of the same norm: -1.6 / -4.7 %. A constant on the MLP output only: 14.0 / 15.1 %, i.e. 17-21 % of what all MLP weights close (67.7 / 86.4 %), so 'the MLP change is mostly a constant vector' is refuted. The 472 always-on neurons (0.13 % of 352,256; 110 in the last layer) copied from RL close 2.6 / 3.4 %, vs 0.1-0.2 % for 472 other neurons. Picture: RL = a fixed, direction-specific push per layer (about a quarter to a third) + small input-dependent changes over almost every neuron. Controls passed. Limit: teacher-forced distance to RL, not accuracy. Job sameraslan-1114-184552-a899 (H100, 6 min), commit a2ec2c9.
